description: Nous sommes une équipe motivée par l’exploration spatiale et la recherche scientifique. Notre objectif est de participer au challenge visant à identifier sur Terre des lieux présentant des caractéristiques analogues aux environnements de la Lune et de Mars, afin de contribuer à la préparation de futures missions spatiales.
summary:
From to Mars: Earth Analog Sites

Our project explores how selected environments on Earth can help us understand and prepare for future human and robotic exploration of the Moon and Mars.

Through an interactive digital platform, Lunar Mars Explorers presents and compares terrestrial sites with relevant planetary characteristics, including the McMurdo Dry Valleys, Dallol, Vredefort, Lompoul Desert and Lake Retba. Each location offers a different scientific perspective, from extreme cold and aridity to geological structures, mineral environments and saline conditions.

Using geographic information, scientific literature, satellite observations and available space-agency datasets, we investigate the similarities and differences between these terrestrial environments and selected lunar and Martian conditions. Our platform combines maps, site descriptions, scientific evidence and visual comparisons to make these complex environments easier to explore.

A key part of our project is highlighting Senegal's potential contribution to planetary analog research by examining environments such as the Desert and Lake Retba. These sites are presented as exploratory candidates whose scientific relevance must be assessed through evidence, not assumed from appearance alone.

Our goal is not to claim that Earth can perfectly reproduce another world, but to show how carefully selected terrestrial environments can support research, mission preparation and scientific understanding Moon and Mars
details: Project Details 1. What does our project do and how does it work? From Lompoul to Mars: Earth Analog Sites is an interactive web-based platform designed to explore terrestrial environments that may provide useful scientific analogies for the Moon and Mars. The platform brings together information on 15 terrestrial environments across seven scientific themes, including impact structures, volcanism, cryospheric environments, evaporites, dunes, astrobiology and geological structures. Users can explore different locations through an interactive atlas, access scientific descriptions of selected sites, examine their geographical characteristics and understand their potential relevance to planetary exploration. Our approach combines geographical information, scientific literature, environmental observations and available satellite data to investigate similarities and differences between Earth environments and extraterrestrial conditions. 2. What benefits does it have? The project makes scientific information about planetary analog environments more accessible and organized. It helps users: - Explore terrestrial environments that can support planetary research. - Understand how geographical, geological and climatic conditions influence the selection of exploration sites. - Compare different types of environments rather than relying on visual similarities alone. - Discover potential research opportunities in regions that receive less attention, particularly in Africa. 3. What is the intended impact? Our main objective is to contribute to the understanding of how Earth environments can support the preparation of future lunar and Martian exploration missions. We also aim to highlight Senegal's scientific potential through the study of the Lompoul Desert and Lake Retba. These locations are presented as exploratory candidates whose relevance must be evaluated through scientific evidence. In the long term, the project could serve as an educational and research-oriented resource for students, researchers and people interested in planetary science, geography and space exploration. 4. What tools and technologies did we use? We developed an interactive web platform and a scientific report using digital development tools, programming and data analysis. Our work involved: - Web development and interactive visualization. - Python-based data processing and analysis. - Geographical and satellite data exploration. - Scientific research using publications and space-agency resources. - Artificial intelligence tools, including DeepSeek and Claude, to assist with coding, development and research-related tasks. AI-generated assistance was reviewed by the team, and scientific information was considered against available sources. 5. How is our project creative? The originality of our project lies in combining an interactive digital atlas with a comparative scientific approach. Instead of presenting isolated locations, we organize environments according to different scientific characteristics and explain both their potential analogies and their limitations. Another distinctive aspect is our inclusion of Senegalese environments in a planetary-science investigation. This creates an opportunity to connect local geographical knowledge with international space exploration research. 6. What factors did our team consider? Our team considered several scientific and practical factors when exploring potential analog sites: - Geological characteristics and surface materials. - Topography and geographical location. - Climate and temperature conditions. - Aridity, salinity and extreme environmental conditions. - Mineralogical and biological characteristics where information was available. - The availability and reliability of scientific and satellite data. - The limitations of terrestrial analogies compared with the actual environments of the Moon and Mars. We recognize that no terrestrial environment can perfectly reproduce another planetary body. Therefore, our project focuses on identifying useful similarities while clearly acknowledging scientific differences and limitations.
